$description:
THIS FILE HELD NO TOKENS BETWEEN 2026-08-15 AND 2026-08-16, and the record of why is kept below because it is what makes the one token now here defensible. Two height ramps have lived here and both are gone; nothing in the kit states a height as a token any more, and `target-size.min` below is NOT one — read the FLOOR IS NOT A RAMP note on it before touching it.

`control-height` (28/32/40/48px) went on 2026-08-14. A fixed px height cannot grow with its contents: the text inside an input or a button is sized in `rem` via a `clamp()`, so it grows with a user's browser font-size preference, with a spoke's taller face, or when a translation wraps — and a px box cannot follow. `esa-text-field` paired that fixed height with `overflow: hidden`, so what did not fit was silently cut, which is WCAG 1.4.4 (Resize text). Padding cannot fail that way: whatever the line box turns out to be, the padding still surrounds it.

`chip-height` (18/22/28/34px) went on 2026-08-15, and it is the more interesting deletion because it did not fail — it was hiding something. It was read by four components through four tier-3 hooks (`--badge-height-*`, `--pill-height-*`, `--chip-group-height-*`, `--filter-pill-height`), which is a real agreement and a defensible tier-2 intent. What it was agreeing ON was the problem: badge, pill, chip-group and filter-pills each wear a DIFFERENT type rung at the same nominal size (label-sm-strong, label-sm, label-md-strong and a fixed label-xs respectively), and the shared height was overriding that disagreement so a row still lined up. The token was compensating for a typography inconsistency, one tier away from where the inconsistency lives.

THE ARITHMETIC THAT SETTLED IT, worth keeping because it is not obvious. Every rung on the spacing scale is an even number of px, so padding contributes a multiple of 4 to a height. At the clamp plateau the four components' font sizes are 14, 14, 15 and 12px — residues 2, 3 and 0 mod 4. Padding cannot change a residue, so once these are sized by padding + text, NO choice of spacing rungs makes any two of them equal while their type rungs differ. That is why the height token could not simply be swapped for a padding token, and why the type rungs are the actual fix. Aligning them is a separate pass.

WHAT REPLACED IT is padding on both axes, walking the rung each component's `padding-inline` already used — the pattern `esa-button` settled on when `control-height` went (`--_btn-pad-y` equals `--_btn-padding-x` at every size). Heights are therefore fluid now, as the inputs' are, and are whatever the line box plus that padding resolves to.

CONSEQUENCE TO BE CLEAR ABOUT: there is no one-line height lever for a spoke at any tier for these four, and re-declaring any of the seventeen retired names does nothing. Re-pointing `--spacing-*` moves every gap in the kit, because it is a CORE set. Tightening a chip is a /request-lego.

CARRIED FORWARD FOR THE BATCHED ACCESSIBILITY PASS: `xs` and `sm` chips were 18px and 22px, below the WCAG 2.5.8 AA minimum of 24px, and esa-chip-group is interactive. Padding sizing does not fix that on its own — it changes the numbers without raising them past 24px — so the observation survives the deletion and still needs actioning. That is what `target-size.min` now actions.

Do NOT re-add a height token. If something looks wrong, the padding or the type rung is the thing to change.

min.$description:
The enforced minimum hit area for an interactive control, read as `min-block-size` / `min-inline-size` by the components' hit areas. Zero by default, so it is INERT in every build that does not opt in; the accessibility assurance profile re-points it (`[data-assurance="wcag-aa"]` sets 24px, the WCAG 2.2 SC 2.5.8 AA floor). A spoke wanting the 2.5.5 AAA floor sets 44px in its own scope.

FLOOR IS NOT A RAMP, and this is the whole reason this token is allowed to exist in a file whose $description ends 'Do NOT re-add a height token'. The objection that killed `control-height` was that a FIXED px height cannot grow with its contents, so `esa-text-field` clipped rem text under `overflow: hidden` — WCAG 1.4.4. A `min-block-size` has the opposite failure mode by construction: it raises the bottom and does nothing to the top, so the box still grows with the line box, with a user's font-size preference, with a taller face and with a wrapping translation. There is no value of this token that can clip anything. It is also ONE name, not a four-step ramp, so it cannot be used as the density lever the retired ramps were misused as — 'make the controls tighter' is still a /request-lego.

WHY IT IS DECLARED AT ALL RATHER THAN LEFT TO THE PROFILE. A component reading `var(--target-size-min, 0px)` would work with no declaration anywhere, but then the name would exist only inside the profile block and in 20-odd component files, which is exactly the shape that goes stale: nothing would list it, `token-names.json` would not baseline it, and a rename would not be caught. Declared here it is a shipped name under the same guard as every other.

REPLACES `--touch-target-min` (44px, removed 2026-08-16), which named this role one tier up and was read by nothing — see `touch-target-min-to-target-size-min` in migrations.json for why a constant could not simply be aliased onto a lever.
